title: Who carries the signs the known cases carried
question: Among organizations that are in no case file, which carry most of the signs that marked the known cases before they became public?
finding: This is a way to choose where to look first; it is not evidence about any organization. 605 organizations in no case file carry at least one of the 21 informative signs; the highest weighted count is 8 of a possible 23, held by Bayview Opera House, and the fiftieth is 2. The known-case organizations themselves have a middle figure of 1 on the same sum, and 605 organizations outside any case file match or exceed it. The highest-scoring fifty received $3.53 billion from the City in fiscal 2019 to 2026.
how: The score is the number of informative signs an organization carries today, each counted at its weight from the previous screen: Monitoring findings left open in three or more years, or published targets missed = 2; Monitoring findings left unresolved two years running = 2; A State grant and a City contract for the same kind of work = 1; A gift or donation within 90 days before a decision by an official who decided, sponsored or voted on it (this file) = 1; A gift, donation or requested payment in the year one of its contracts was approved = 1; A name match between its staff and the payroll of the department that funds it, near a contract (this file) = 1; Agreements that at least doubled through amendments = 1; Agreements that grew past their first ceiling = 1; An audit on file, and a return that says none was required = 1; Identical odd amounts paid twice in one year = 1; One owner, several names, all paid by the City = 1; Paid more the year after falling short = 1; Paid three ways: City, State and federal money in the same year = 1; Returns that say a federal audit was required, with no audit on file = 1; Returns that were amended, or that changed the rules they are kept by = 1; The few add-back lines that name an organisation = 1; Three or more kinds of dated dealing with one official inside two years (this file) = 1; Two or more contracts approved after the work began = 1; Two or more contracts sized just under the $10 million line = 1; Who bills for whose services = 1; Yearly reports to the State that the organization's own tax return contradicts = 1. Only signs that were datable before at least two known cases became public are used. Organizations named in any case file at any level, including leads, are left out.
limits: A high score means only that an organization shares recorded features with a small, unrepresentative set of known cases. The features are mostly those of large nonprofits funded under emergency or waiver rules and monitored by the Controller, so the score partly ranks size, the pandemic years and how closely an organization has been watched. The weights rest on a few dozen cases and would shift if one case were added or removed. The score is deliberately not attached to any organization as a warning sign. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
